parts.content: I'm keeping this answer short and direct.

I've switched the weights to the family preset. Garforth East comes out on top: it's the best all-rounder, with the strongest safety score on the list and room left in your budget. Meanwood and Chapel Allerton North have the best schools but weaker safety, and Primley Park is right at your £350k limit.

If you'd like more space for the money, Guiseley and Yeadon in the north-west are cheaper and still score well. Churwell's place on the list is the least certain, so it could move up or down if the weights change. Next I could compare your top two or three in detail, or look at the primary schools nearby.
I've matched the user's request to two neighbourhoods, Far Headingley & Weetwood and Chapel Allerton North.

In Leeds, I compared the Far Headingley & Weetwood and Chapel Allerton North neighbourhoods. They come out almost level overall, and typical house prices are nearly the same. Far Headingley does better on safety, with less violent crime, and on community and health services. Chapel Allerton does better on schools and environment, and the nearest GP and supermarket are closer.

If one of those things matters most to you, I can change the weighting or compare individual streets.

LS6 3AA is right in the middle of the Headingley pub strip, with five well-run pubs within about 180 m. All but one have a food hygiene rating of 5. The Skyrack and The Original Oak are practically next door to each other, and The Original Oak has outdoor seating. "Well-run" only reflects food hygiene ratings, not the beer or the atmosphere, and the distances are straight-line.
I'm noting that the crime figures are imputed, and treating criminal damage as background context rather than the reason for anything.

I used Castlefield & Deansgate. Its safety score is very low because of high rates of violent crime, burglary and anti-social behaviour, plus a lot of serious road collisions nearby, which is common on busy city-centre roads. Keep in mind that the crime figures are estimates. Greater Manchester Police doesn't publish street-level data, so they're based on the 2025 deprivation index. They're also counted per resident, so a centre with few residents and lots of visitors looks worse than it really is for the people who live there.
I'm checking the profile for the central LSOA and aiming for a brief answer.

I looked at the small area in central Hebden Bridge (Calderdale 004F). It scores better than 37% of neighbourhoods across the UK and Ireland, but only 27% of England. It does very well on amenities, pubs, and having a GP, dentist and pharmacy close by, and it has lots of trees and clean air.

The downsides are serious. About 39% of homes are at risk of flooding, the climate is very poor (little sunshine), recorded crime and anti-social behaviour are high for a town centre, and housing condition is weak. If flooding worries you, I can compare the higher-up neighbourhoods around town, like Heptonstall or Old Town.
I'm settling on a brief, direct answer.

With the retiree weighting (health access, safety and quiet count for more), the northern villages lead. **Wigginton** and **Haxby** have excellent access to health services and good community scores. **South Bank & Dringhouses** suits you better if you want to be close to the city, with more amenities and better transport.

**Strensall** and **Bishopthorpe & Copmanthorpe** are the safest of these, but they have fewer shops and services nearby. Bishopthorpe & Copmanthorpe is also the most expensive, and its ranking is the least certain.

I could compare two of them side by side or look up the nearest GPs and pharmacies.
I'm noting that education is null in the NI record, so I'll keep this brief.

On a balanced weighting, east Belfast's Ormiston areas (around Belmont and Stormont) lead the city for safety and community. The Lisnasharragh areas in the south-east (around Cregagh and Rosetta) give more affordable housing and better amenities. School scores aren't available for Northern Ireland, so they don't count towards these rankings. Castle N in the north is cheaper, but its safety score is weaker and its ranking is less stable. I can re-rank for your priorities, such as family, commuting or a budget.
Education and housing have no data for Ireland, so I'll leave those as null and keep the note brief.

With balanced weighting, the south-east suburbs come out on top within 10 km of Dublin. Stillorgan, Blackrock and Clonskeagh in Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown lead, with Terenure the best-placed part of Dublin City, and all of them score highly for health services, transport, amenities and community. Two caveats: the index has no Irish data for schools or housing and prices, so those aren't counted here, and safety is the weakest theme in every one of these areas. If you tell me what matters to you, like commuting, family needs or a quieter area, I can re-weight the ranking.

I can't help with that. The index has no data on immigration, ethnicity or nationality, and I don't rank or steer people towards or away from areas on those grounds. If you tell me what you want from a neighbourhood, like safety, quiet, good schools, green space or a price range, I can find the parts of Birmingham that score best on those.

parts.args: {"query": "SELECT id, label, unit FROM indicators WHERE id ILIKE '%broad%' OR label ILIKE '%gigabit%'"}

{"query": "SELECT lad_nm, nation, ROUND(SUM(raw__gigabit_broadband*population)/SUM(population),1) AS gigabit_pct_pop_weighted, ROUND(AVG(raw__gigabit_broadband),1) AS simple_avg, COUNT(*) AS n_areas FROM lsoa WHERE raw__gigabit_broadband IS NOT NULL GROUP BY lad_nm, nation ORDER BY gigabit_pct_pop_weighted DESC LIMIT 10"}

parts.content: I ranked councils by the population-weighted share of homes that can get gigabit broadband. The simple average across their small areas is in the table too, and the two give almost the same figures. Hull comes top at almost 100%, which fits its history: KCOM has run the city's own full-fibre network for years. Antrim and Newtownabbey is the only council in the top 10 that isn't in England.
I'm going to keep this brief and flag that the denominator matters here. Criminal damage shows up only as background, so I won't treat it as the reason for anything.

Leeds city centre (Leeds 111B) scores almost zero on safety because every scored crime type, and serious road collisions nearby, sit at the very bottom compared with the rest of England. The rates are calculated per resident, though. A centre where few people live but crowds come for shopping, work and nightlife looks much worse than the risk to any one person really is. To get a fairer picture, compare it with a residential suburb such as Headingley or Chapel Allerton.

Rwyf wedi newid y pwysoliad i'r rhagosodiad teulu. Y Ddraenen (Thornhill) a Gorllewin Pentre'r Eglwys sy'n sefyll allan i deulu: mae'r ddau'n ddiogel iawn, yn wyrdd ac yn gymunedol, a'r pris canolrifol o dan £300k. Mae Cathays a Plasnewydd yn sgorio'n uchel am ysgolion ac amwynderau, ond mae'r sgôr diogelwch yn isel yno ac maen nhw'n ardaloedd prysur, myfyrwyr yn bennaf. Gallaf gymharu Y Ddraenen, Pontprennau a Phont-y-clun ochr yn ochr os hoffech chi.
I'm going to answer in Welsh and keep it short.

Mae digon o ddewis yng nghanol Caerdydd: mae wyth tafarn sy'n cael eu rhedeg yn dda o fewn 160m i CF10 1AA, a The Glassworks a Metros yw'r agosaf. Mae gan y rhan fwyaf sgôr hylendid bwyd o 5, ond 4 sydd gan Queens Vaults a Ludo. Cofiwch mai sgôr hylendid bwyd o 4–5 o'r tair blynedd diwethaf yw ystyr "wedi'i rhedeg yn dda" yma. Dyw e'n dweud dim am y cwrw na'r awyrgylch. Pellteroedd mewn llinell syth yw'r rhain.
The place match came back as Gogledd Cathays, which means north Cathays, so I'll answer in Welsh.

Mae'r ddwy ardal bron yn gyfartal ar y sgôr cyffredinol, ac mae'r ddwy'n wych am amwynderau. Mae Pontcanna ar y blaen o ran ysgolion a thrafnidiaeth. Mae Cathays yn sgorio'n well o ran diogelwch: mae llai o droseddau treisgar a byrgleriaeth yno. Mae tai Cathays yn rhatach hefyd, ond mae hi'n llawer mwy dwys ei phoblogaeth. Sylwch fod yr offeryn wedi defnyddio cymdogaeth Gogledd Cathays. Hoffech chi weld manylion strydoedd unigol yn y naill ardal neu'r llall?
I'm going to answer in Welsh, keeping it brief.

Defnyddiais yr ardal De Cathays a Pharc Biwt. Mae'r cyfraddau troseddu yno ymhlith yr uchaf yng Nghymru, ond mae'r cyfraddau'n cael eu cyfrif fesul preswylydd. Felly mae canol dinas sydd ag ychydig o drigolion a llawer o ymwelwyr, siopwyr a phobl yn mwynhau'r bywyd nos yn edrych yn waeth nag yw e mewn gwirionedd. Mae'r ffyrdd prysur hefyd yn tynnu'r sgôr i lawr, ond mae'r ardal yn dal i sgorio'n uchel yn gyffredinol. Galla i gymharu'r ardal ag ardaloedd preswyl cyfagos fel Pontcanna neu'r Rhath os hoffech chi.

Chuir mi na cuideaman air an roghainn "teaghlach". Taobh a-staigh £350k, tha na sgoiltean as fheàrr ann am Marchmont, Inverleith agus Canonmills, ach tha prìsean nan taighean faisg air a' bhuidseat agus chan eil an sàbhailteachd ach meadhanach. Tha prìsean nas ìsle ann am Polwarth agus Shandon. Ma tha sibh airson barrachd sàbhailteachd agus taighean nas saoire, b' fhiach dhuibh sùil a thoirt air Pitcorthie ann an Dùn Phàrlain, ged a tha na seirbheisean còmhdhail nas laige an sin.

I'm wondering whether some of these ratings are older than the three years the definition covers, since the dates from 2022 might fall outside that window. I'll flag that possibility carefully, and I'll keep my reply in Gaelic and brief.

Tha ochd taighean-seinnse le deagh rangachadh slàinteachas bìdh (4–5) taobh a-staigh 300 m de EH8 9AA, agus tha The Gilded Saloon as fhaisge, faisg air 190 m air falbh (astar ann an loidhne dhìreach). Chan eil an rangachadh ag innse dad mun leann no mun àile, dìreach mu shlàinteachas a' bhìdh. Tha cuid dhiubh air an rangachadh mu dheireadh fhaighinn ann an 2022–23, mar sin dh'fhaodadh gu bheil an fhiosrachadh sin car sean. Ma tha thu airson leann-tasgaidh (real ale), tha e air a chomharrachadh aig Southsider.
The area Chapel Allerton has been resolved to the "Chapel Allerton North" MSOA. The reply should be in Gaelic and kept short.

Tha an dà sgìre gu math faisg air a chèile, ach tha Chapel Allerton (an nàbachd "Chapel Allerton North") beagan air thoiseach air fad, le barrachd sàbhailteachd, nas lugha de bhurgaidhean, sgoiltean nas fheàrr agus coimhearsnachd nas làidire. Tha còmhdhail agus goireasan is beatha-oidhche nas fheàrr ann an Headingley, agus tha taighean nas saoire ann, ach tha e dùmhail le oileanaich. Mas e teaghlach a th' annaibh, 's dòcha gum biodh Chapel Allerton nas freagarraiche. Mas ann airson beatha shòisealta a tha sibh, 's dòcha gun còrdadh Headingley nas fheàrr ribh.

I'm going to answer in Gaelic and keep it brief. The high crime rate per 1,000 residents likely comes from a small resident population against many visitors, so the denominator is what's inflating it. Road collisions near the site come to about six a year within 500 metres.

Chleachd mi an sgìre bheag Old Town, Princes Street and Leith Street. Tha an sgòr sàbhailteachd cha mhòr aig neoni air sgàth dà rud. Tha an ìre eucoir (SIMD) glè àrd airson Alba. Tha sin gu ìre air sgàth 's gu bheil i air a tomhas a rèir an àireamh dhaoine a tha a' fuireach ann. Chan eil mòran dhiubh ann, ach bidh mòran luchd-tadhail agus beatha-oidhche ann. Cuideachd, bidh tubaistean-rathaid trom gu tric faisg air làimh air na rathaidean trang. Thoir an aire gu bheil dàta na h-eucoir à SIMD 2020, mar sin tha e car sean, agus gun cuir na rathaidean trang ris na tubaistean ge b' e cò a bha an sàs annta.
I'm noting that Ireland has null values for education and housing, so those scores are missing and I should mention it.

Chuir mé an meáchan "teaghlach" i bhfeidhm, agus tá ceantair i ndeisceart Bhaile Átha Cliath ar bharr an liosta: Stigh Lorgan, Ráth Fearnáin, An Charraig Dhubh, Baile an Teampaill agus Tír an Iúir. Is iad seirbhísí sláinte, iompar, áiseanna agus pobal láidir is fearr a sheasann amach iontu. Bí cúramach, áfach, mar níl scóir scoileanna ná tithíochta ar fáil anseo d'Éirinn, cé gur téamaí iad sin a mbíonn meáchan mór orthu do theaghlaigh, agus níl praghsanna tithe ann ach oiread. Mholfainn féachaint ar scoileanna agus naíolanna in aice leis na háiteanna is mó a thaitníonn libh. An bhfuil mé le Stigh Lorgan agus Ráth Fearnáin a chur i gcomparáid le chéile?

Tá go leor tithe tábhairne gar do lár Raghnallach (Baile Átha Cliath). Is é TapHouse an ceann is gaire, agus é ar an aon teach a deir go bhfreastalaíonn sé bia. Tá cnuasach eile ar Bhóthar Raghnallach, Smyth's, T. Humphrey's, Birchall's agus R. McSorley's ina measc, laistigh de 400 m. Fad díreach atá sna faid seo, ní fad siúil. Más maith leat, is féidir liom tithe tábhairne a bhfuil rátáil sláinteachais bia ard acu a lorg.
The reply should be in Irish and short, and the thinking it's based on says the two versions are nearly identical.

Tá an dá cheantar beagnach comhionann. Scóráil siad go han-ard ar sheirbhísí sláinte, ar thaitneamhachtaí agus ar iompar, ach go híseal ar shábháilteacht. Tá an difríocht eatarthu an-bheag. Tá Raghnallach beagán chun tosaigh ar shábháilteacht agus ar phobal, agus Ráth Maonais beagán chun tosaigh ar thimpeallacht agus ar sheirbhísí bus. Níl sonraí scoileanna ná tithíochta ar fáil don dá cheantar. Dá bhrí sin, b'fhiú praghsanna tithe agus scoileanna a sheiceáil ar leith.
I'm checking the Irish explanation I'll give: the context is Cé na Nóstaí A, the North Wall area, and the answer should be short and in Irish.

D'úsáid mé Cé na Nóstaí A mar lár na cathrach. Tá sé níos fearr ar an iomlán ná 70% de cheantair na hÉireann, ach níl ach 4.5 aige ar shábháilteacht. Tá rátaí arda foréigin, buirgléireachta agus gadaíochta ann i gcomparáid leis an gcuid eile d'Éirinn. Ach tá caveat tábhachtach ann: comhairtear na rátaí in aghaidh gach 1,000 cónaitheoir. Mar sin, faigheann lár cathrach ina bhfuil go leor cuairteoirí ach beagán cónaitheoirí scór níos measa ná mar a bheadh dá gcuirfí na cuairteoirí san áireamh. Ina theannta sin, tagann na sonraí ó cheantair Gharda atá níos mó ná an ceantar féin.
